claims.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
claims.evidence: The scan marks exactly the descent bottoms. The marked elements are moved in increasing original-index order, so successive MoveToFront operations reverse their order. Unmarked elements are never removed and retain their relative order. An independent literal queue-and-MoveToFront implementation agreed with the formula on every permutation through size 9.
claims.search_method: Deductive operational analysis plus exhaustive comparison of independently implemented literal and closed-form round maps on every permutation of sizes 1 through 9.

claims.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
claims.evidence: Element i cannot be marked. If R is nonempty, its first entry is marked because it follows i, while r_j for j>=2 remains to the right of i exactly when r_{j-1}<r_j. Claim 0 preserves the order of these survivors, so the next right word is exactly A(R), independently of L. The already-fixed larger suffix remains fixed. Iteration gives the stated extinction time, including h(empty)=0 without an off-by-one error. Exhaustive literal simulation confirmed both the one-round invariant and full phase duration for every active-prefix permutation through size 9; iterative extinction also agreed with the monotone-stack computation.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof plus exhaustive testing of every active-prefix permutation through size 9 and every permutation word through length 9.

claims.claim: If W(n) is the worst-case number of nontrivial rounds, then W(n)<=n(n-1)/2. Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
claims.evidence: The phases for maxima n,n-1,...,2 cover the execution, with zero duration when a maximum is already fixed. In the i-phase, |R|<=i-1 and each application of A to a nonempty word reduces its length by at least one, so h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. Summing gives W(n)<=sum_{i=2}^n(i-1)=n(n-1)/2. Hence every family's round count divided by n^2 is bounded above by (n-1)/(2n), ruling out omega(n^2). The bound was also checked on every permutation through n=9.
claims.search_method: General phase-sum proof plus exhaustive counterexample search and bound verification through n=9.

claims.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
claims.evidence: With B_0 empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m), induction using Claim 0 gives T^t(p_n)=B_t,n,t+1,...,n-1 for 0<=t<=n-1, so n first becomes fixed after n-1 rounds. Put m=n-1. A direct induction over m=q(q+1)/2+r, 0<=r<=q, gives maximum deletion label q for B_m, where q(q+1)<=2m<(q+1)(q+2); the explicit consecutive-value stack invariant in the draft has exactly that maximum. Since B_m=mT(B_{m-1}) and m>=2, A(B_m)=A(T(B_{m-1})), so the next maximum requires exactly q additional rounds. This proves the claimed lower bound. Integer checks validated the labeled-stack invariant through m=1000 and the complete trajectory and second-phase duration through n=200.
claims.witness: The family p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1), checked exactly for every 3<=n<=200.
claims.search_method: Induction on the special trajectory and triangular blocks, supplemented by exact-integer checks of B_m through m=1000 and full trajectories through n=200.

claims.claim: Under the zero-no-op-round convention, the exact worst-case values for n=1,...,9 are 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
claims.evidence: Complete enumeration of all 409113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9 recovered maxima [0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26]. Every unsorted transition was checked to be nontrivial, with cycle detection. For n=2 through 8, (n,1,...,n-1) attains the listed value; for n=9, (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) takes 26 rounds. Exhaustion supplies the matching upper bounds.
claims.witness: Attainment witnesses are (1) for n=1, (n,1,...,n-1) for 2<=n<=8, and (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) for n=9.
claims.search_method: Complete enumeration of sum_{n=1}^9 n! = 409113 permutations using exact tuple operations and cycle detection.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an asymptotically tight worst-case round count and particularly asks whether any family requires omega(n^2) rounds. The verified quadratic upper bound conclusively answers the highlighted omega(n^2) subquestion in the negative and is material progress. However, the retained all-n lower bound is only Theta(n), while the upper bound is O(n^2); finite values through n=9 do not close that asymptotic gap. The final writeup explicitly says the tight order remains open and claims only PARTIAL resolution. Thus the target is not fully resolved, but the claimed resolution is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and revision draft; no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior frontier run, verification report, or other solution was accessed.
Compared the closed round formula with a separately implemented literal mark-all-then-sequential-MoveToFront operation on all 409113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9.
Checked the autonomous maximum-phase equation and exact extinction duration on all 409113 active-prefix permutations through size 9.
Compared iterative A-extinction with the monotone-stack computation on 409114 words, comprising the empty word and every permutation word through length 9.
Exhaustively recovered W(1),...,W(9)=0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26 and checked the phase-sum upper bound for every enumerated permutation.
Checked the special B_m deletion-height and full labeled-stack invariant through m=1000, and checked complete special-family trajectories and lower bounds through n=200.
Used only integer arithmetic for decisions, including integer square root and the exact inequalities q(q+1)<=2m<(q+1)(q+2); no floating-point decision was used.
